functions.funcDef: Provide propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (§5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans provide thrust for all flight phases (§5.1.1); independent per engine, one-engine-out continuation at/after V1 (§5.1.3).

functions.funcDef: Provide propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (§5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Thrust reversers on the two inboard engines, inhibited in flight by WOW and radio-altimeter agreement (§5.1.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to achieve control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (§5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers, ailerons on HYD B and C (§5.3.2); independent of pitch/yaw axes.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to achieve control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (§5.3.1).
functions.subDef: All-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser with elevators on HYD A and C, with mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim (§5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to achieve control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (§5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Split upper/lower rudder, each on its own actuation and hydraulic supply (A upper, B lower); sizing case is outboard engine-out at V1 with max blade (§5.3.2, §5.3.3).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to achieve control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (§5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span slats via two PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (§5.3.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and provide braking and ground directional control (§5.6.1).
functions.subDef: One nose unit and six main bogies (20 tyres) absorb landing/taxi loads and spread footprint for flotation on semi-prepared surfaces; leg/bogie count preliminary (§5.6.1, §5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and provide braking and ground directional control (§5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Retraction/extension on HYD A with free-fall alternate; dual independent downlock sensing (§5.6.2, §5.6.3).

functions.funcName: Support and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and provide braking and ground directional control (§5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking normally HYD B, alternate HYD A, with accumulator emergency reserve sized to six applications; per-wheel-pair anti-skid (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control the aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and provide braking and ground directional control (§5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2).

functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in access for a single blade and restrain the payload through all flight and ground load cases (§5.7.1, §5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Upward-hinging nose visor opened/closed on HYD A with electric backup; twelve latches on common torque shaft, eight lock pins on a separate supply, dual dissimilar sensing, pressure interlock (§5.7.2). Excludes the door structural load path (§5.7.3, treated as structure).

functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in access for a single blade and restrain the payload through all flight and ground load cases (§5.7.1, §5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Nine saddles with two tensioned straps each, electric winches locked mechanically, single instrumented tension monitoring loop (§5.8.2). Hold floor hard points treated as structure (§5.8.3).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (§5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two air-cycle packs fed from four engines via a cross-bleed manifold; separate flight-deck and hold conditioning zones (§5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (§5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two digital controllers driving two outflow valves with pneumatic backup; independent positive/negative relief; hold differential preliminary (§5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice on surfaces, inlets and probes for the icing envelope of the cert basis (§5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect surfaces and inlets from ice
functions.subDef: Bleed-air protection to wing leading edges and engine cowls via piccolo; six independently controlled electrically heated stabiliser zones (§5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice on surfaces, inlets and probes for the icing envelope of the cert basis (§5.10.1).
functions.subDef: Electrically heated probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors, individually monitored; detection advisory with automatic activation (§5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host alerting (§5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Four display units, two HUDs driven by three display processors on dual networks; three air-data inertial reference units; independent standby instrument on DC essential (§5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host alerting (§5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, driven by two independent processing channels (§5.11.2).

functions.funcName: Protect against fire and provide crew oxygen
functions.funcDef: Detect and extinguish fire/overheat where required, and supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew (§5.12.1, §5.13.1).
functions.subName: Detect and extinguish fire and overheat
functions.subDef: Dual-loop nacelle/APU detection with AND-to-single degradation; two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed; bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat; hold smoke detection with no suppression (§5.12.2).

functions.funcName: Protect against fire and provide crew oxygen
functions.funcDef: Detect and extinguish fire/overheat where required, and supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew (§5.12.1, §5.13.1).
functions.subDef: Two HP cylinders on a common manifold with crossover feeding four quick-donning demand masks for depressurisation/smoke/fume events (§5.13.2).

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous forward thrust — thrust delivered differs from the commanded value (wrong magnitude in response to command)
fha.effAc: Thrust does not match commanded value on one or more engines; if erroneous on an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm the resulting asymmetry challenges directional control, the sizing case for rudder authority. Trajectory and speed control degraded; at take-off/landing the effect on flight-path and directional control is most severe.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the mismatch via engine parameter displays and aircraft response and must intervene (retard/manage the affected engine, apply rudder). Increased workload during a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous thrust on an outboard engine produces the asymmetry the airframe is sized against; an out-of-tolerance case during take-off/landing gives a large reduction in safety margins with high crew workload to control the flight path. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded forward thrust — thrust delivered on one or more engines with no crew command
fha.effAc: Thrust appears without command; if on an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm it drives asymmetry against which directional control is sized. Uncommanded thrust during approach/landing degrades deceleration and flight-path control.
fha.effCrew: Crew become aware through engine displays and aircraft response and must isolate the affected engine (fuel shut-off/fire handle) and counter the asymmetry; increased workload at a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded thrust from an outboard engine loads the directional-control sizing case and reduces safety margins in the take-off/landing phases with elevated crew workload; effects stated support Hazardous. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust — asymmetric (thrust reduced on one side)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust from a partial loss on one side; loss of an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the directional-control sizing case, and the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at or after V1. Reduced climb/performance and a directional-control demand.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the loss and asymmetry via engine displays and aircraft response, apply rudder and manage remaining engines per engine-out procedure; increased workload, particularly at/after V1.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric partial thrust loss on an outboard engine is the case the directional control is sized against; a large reduction in safety margins with high crew workload in the take-off phase supports Hazardous, while the design accommodates single-engine loss. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust — asymmetric (duplicate id; distinct condition to be confirmed)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric partial thrust loss on one side; loss of an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the directional-control sizing case. Reduced performance and a directional-control demand; the distinct scope of this second condition versus SF-001-PL is not established from the provided material.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the asymmetry via engine displays and aircraft response and manage it per engine-out procedure; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This id duplicates SF-001-PL with identical text; the distinguishing degradation (which engines, magnitude, or a second-engine-same-side case explicitly retained as a condition to be studied) is not grounded in the provided material, so the aircraft effect that would drive the class cannot be stated. Confirm whether this collapses into SF-001-PL or represents the two-engines-same-side case before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust — thrust unavailable from all four engines
fha.effAc: No propulsive thrust from any engine; the aircraft cannot sustain powered flight and cannot continue to a suitable aerodrome under power. Symmetric loss, so no thrust asymmetry, but the aircraft is committed to an unpowered descent/forced landing.
fha.effCrew: Crew face maximum workload managing a total loss of thrust and an unpowered descent/forced-landing outside the design dispatch case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of thrust from all four engines removes powered flight and the ability to reach a suitable aerodrome, resulting in loss of the airplane; the effects support Catastrophic. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent ground deceleration thrust (symmetric reverser/deceleration thrust when not commanded)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded deceleration during take-off roll degrades acceleration and can prevent achieving V1 within available distance; symmetric event is directionally controllable but reduces takeoff performance margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects unexpected deceleration and reverser/deceleration cues; rejects take-off or manages the roll — increased workload during a high-workload phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Symmetric inadvertent ground deceleration is directionally manageable but produces a significant reduction in take-off performance margin and a significant increase in crew workload during take-off/landing. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded ground deceleration thrust — asymmetric (deceleration thrust on one side only, uncommanded)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric uncommanded deceleration produces a yawing moment during the ground roll; on a semi-prepared strip with narrow rollout margin (predicted ~1,080 m against 1,800 m requirement) this can drive a directional excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter the yaw with steering/rudder and reject or manage the roll — high workload; effectiveness depends on speed and surface condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class: the SDD does not quantify the yawing moment from single-side inadvertent inboard-reverser deployment or the resulting excursion at the semi-prepared surface, so whether the outcome is a large or significant reduction in safety margins is not grounded. Also SF-002-M2 is not present in the current FCIM — reconcile the condition before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground deceleration thrust — asymmetric (reduced/asymmetric deceleration thrust available)
fha.effAc: Reduced or asymmetric ground deceleration thrust lengthens rollout and/or induces a yawing moment on a semi-prepared strip; wheel braking (dual hydraulic plus accumulator) remains as the primary stopping means, but the deceleration-thrust contribution to the 1,800 m requirement margin is degraded.
fha.effCrew: Crew applies braking and directional correction; increased workload managing rollout and heading on the strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class: the SDD gives the landing-distance requirement and predicted rollout but does not state the deceleration-thrust share of that margin, so the safety-margin reduction from losing it partially/asymmetrically cannot be grounded without the braking/reverser performance split.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground deceleration thrust (no reverse/deceleration thrust available on landing rollout)
fha.effAc: No deceleration-thrust contribution to the rollout; stopping relies wholly on wheel braking (systems B/A plus six-application accumulator reserve) against the 1,800 m requirement with ~1,080 m predicted rollout. On a semi-prepared surface the erosion of stopping margin could be significant.
fha.effCrew: Crew applies maximum/autobrake and manages rollout within the available distance; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class: the SDD does not state the deceleration-thrust contribution to the accelerate-stop/landing distance, nor the braking-only stopping distance on the semi-prepared surface, so whether losing it entirely is a slight, significant or large reduction in stopping margin is not derivable from the provided material.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll control — response to command (roll surfaces respond incorrectly to pilot/autopilot command, crew aware)
fha.effAc: Erroneous roll response drives an unintended bank/roll rate; on a 160 m span high-wing freighter an uncorrected roll excursion can reach a large reduction in safety margins, and with the maximum blade payload roll-authority margins are set by the loaded case.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceives the erroneous response and counters through the inceptor; degraded control laws are annunciated. Workload and difficulty rise; recovery effectiveness depends on the magnitude of the error.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class without knowing the bounded magnitude/authority of the erroneous roll response — the SDD describes the FBW roll architecture and dissimilar-computer voting but does not state the worst-case erroneous surface excursion, so the aircraft effect (large reduction in margins vs. controllable transient) is not derivable and severity cannot be derived from stated effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be controlled about the roll axis by any means; roll attitude uncontrollable across all phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest bank or maintain wings-level; loss of aircraft control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of roll controllability of the aircraft — loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced roll rate and roll authority; aircraft controllable about roll axis but with reduced margins, aggravated in the engine-out and blade-loaded cases.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain lateral control; degraded law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in safety margins in roll authority with increased crew workload, worst-case at the sizing conditions. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll control — response to command (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Roll response different from that commanded; crew detects the discrepancy via displays/inceptor cues and reverts to a degraded law or mechanical reversion to arrest the erroneous motion.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects abnormal roll response and takes corrective action; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous roll with crew aware and able to counter through degraded control paths — large reduction in safety margins with excessive workload; not committed to Catastrophic because the crew-aware case allows corrective action. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll control — no command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded roll input with no crew or autopilot command; aircraft departs commanded bank.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This turn lists SF-003-M2 but no matching FCIM row exists in the model (SF-003 malfunction rows on file are SF-003-M and SF-003-M3); crew-awareness of the uncommanded input is not stated, so the awareness-dependent effect and severity cannot be grounded. Confirm the intended condition and its awareness split before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous roll control (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Erroneous roll response with no annunciation; crew continue normally and take no corrective action, allowing the erroneous roll to develop toward loss of control.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; no corrective action taken.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected erroneous roll leaves the crew no opportunity to intervene before the aircraft departs controlled flight — loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected uncommanded roll control
fha.effAc: Uncommanded roll input that is not annunciated; crew continue normally and take no corrective action.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; no corrective action taken.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This turn lists SF-003-M4 but no matching FCIM row exists in the model; the distinction from SF-003-M3 (undetected erroneous vs undetected uncommanded) and the source of the uncommanded input are not defined in the provided functions, so the aircraft effect cannot be grounded to a severity. Confirm the intended condition before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch control — surface responds to a pitch command but in the wrong sense or magnitude
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches contrary to or in excess of commanded, departing intended flight path; with a fully-loaded 105 m blade the aircraft may be driven outside its structural/aerodynamic envelope before recovery
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the erroneous response against their command and counter it; correction may be defeated if the FCC command itself is erroneous, forcing degraded-law/mechanical-reversion management under high workload
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous pitch response contrary to command on a primary trajectory function can result in loss of the airplane [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch control — surface moves with no pitch command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded pitch excursion departs the intended flight path with no crew input; runaway of the all-moving stabiliser or elevator can exceed structural/manoeuvre limits with the maximum payload before it is arrested
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion, identify the source and inhibit/counter it; recovery depends on retaining a working command path or reverting to mechanical stabiliser trim
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded pitch runaway on a primary trajectory function can result in loss of the airplane [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous pitch control — erroneous pitch response with no annunciation, crew unaware
fha.effAc: Erroneous pitch response develops without alerting; the crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action, allowing the departure to progress until the aircraft is outside its recoverable envelope
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action against the condition; first cue is aircraft state departure rather than an alert, compressing recognition and recovery time
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected erroneous pitch removes the crew-detection barrier; unarrested departure can result in loss of the airplane [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected uncommanded pitch control — uncommanded pitch motion with no annunciation, crew unaware
fha.effAc: Uncommanded pitch motion develops without alerting; with no crew action the excursion progresses until the aircraft exceeds structural/aerodynamic limits or an unrecoverable attitude
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; recognition depends on noticing an unexplained flight-path change, leaving little time to identify and inhibit the source
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected uncommanded pitch removes the crew-detection barrier; unarrested runaway can result in loss of the airplane [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch authority — degraded response rate/travel; the aircraft remains controllable in pitch but with reduced safety margins, potentially aggravated at forward centre-of-gravity with the maximum-length payload
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain the intended flight path and manage degraded control laws / limited authority through approach and landing
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced pitch authority is a large reduction in safety margins with increased crew workload; confirm against the pitch-authority sizing margins at forward CG with maximum payload [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be controlled about the pitch axis by any means; the trajectory-control function 'Provide pitch control' is wholly lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew have no means of arresting a pitch divergence; flightpath cannot be maintained.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of an axis of trajectory control results in loss of the airplane in every applicable phase. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw control — response to command
fha.effAc: Yaw axis responds incorrectly to command, producing a directional/sideslip upset with the crew aware; degraded but survivable control retained.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the yaw anomaly through heading and sideslip cues and counter it; increased workload to maintain flightpath.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An aware erroneous yaw response is a large reduction in directional safety margins requiring immediate crew action to recover. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw control — no command
fha.effAc: Yaw axis moves without a command, producing an uncommanded directional/sideslip excursion with the crew aware; degraded but survivable control retained.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the uncommanded yaw through heading and sideslip cues and counter it; increased workload to maintain flightpath.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An aware uncommanded yaw excursion is a large reduction in directional safety margins requiring immediate crew action to recover. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous yaw control
fha.effAc: Yaw axis responds incorrectly to command with no indication; crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action, allowing the sideslip/directional divergence to develop unchecked.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the fault; no timely action taken; divergence progresses beyond recoverable limits.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the crew-recovery assumption removed, an undetected erroneous yaw diverges to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected uncommanded yaw control
fha.effAc: Yaw axis moves without command and with no indication; crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action, allowing the directional divergence to develop unchecked.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the fault; no timely action taken; divergence progresses beyond recoverable limits.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the crew-recovery assumption removed, an undetected uncommanded yaw diverges to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced rudder authority narrows the directional-control margin against the sizing case — an outboard engine failure at V1 with maximum blade payload at the 28 m moment arm. Heading may still be held in the nominal case but margin against asymmetric thrust is significantly reduced.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to hold heading and coordinate against reduced authority, particularly in an engine-out approach.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in directional-control safety margin against the stated sizing case (outboard engine-out at V1, max payload, 28 m arm) with increased crew workload — engineer to confirm the margin retained. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of yaw control
fha.effAc: No means of directional control. At the sizing case — an outboard engine failure at V1 with maximum blade payload — the aircraft cannot counter the asymmetric-thrust yawing moment, leading to loss of directional control of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: No rudder authority available; mechanical reversion is to the lower rudder segment only, so total loss removes the crew's directional-control means.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of directional control at the sizing asymmetric-thrust case is loss of the airplane — engineer to confirm against the split-segment architecture that reserves partial authority. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement
fha.effAc: Uncommanded flap or slat movement changes lift and drag against the crew's intent and can produce an out-of-configuration state for the flight phase; the effect on trajectory depends on the direction and magnitude of the movement.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and arrest the uncommanded movement and reconfigure; workload increase in a terminal-area phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states high-lift is driven by two PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes per section, but does not quantify the trajectory effect of an uncommanded symmetric movement (rate, magnitude, phase in which it occurs). Aircraft-level effect cannot be bounded to a single class without that — engineer to supply the high-lift movement authority/rate and worst phase.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift position
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The current FCIM for SF-006 does not carry an 'erroneous high-lift position' condition distinct from uncommanded movement (M) or undetected asymmetry (M3), and the SDD does not describe an aircraft effect specific to a commanded-position error. The condition cannot be distinguished from the uncommanded-movement row on the material provided — engineer to confirm whether M2 is a distinct condition and, if so, its aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected high-lift asymmetry
fha.effAc: An undetected asymmetry between left and right high-lift sections produces an uncommanded rolling moment; with the asymmetry brakes not engaging or the condition progressing unannunciated, the roll can develop while the crew are unaware, degrading the roll-control margin in a configuration-change phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action for the asymmetry itself (unaware case); the first cue is the resulting roll disturbance rather than an asymmetry alert.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD provides asymmetry brakes at each section but does not state the maximum undetected asymmetry that can develop before annunciation or brake engagement, nor the resulting rolling moment. The aircraft-level roll effect cannot be bounded without that limit — engineer to supply the maximum credible undetected asymmetry and its roll authority impact.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of high-lift augmentation — asymmetric
fha.effAc: Asymmetric high-lift produces a rolling moment at low speed with reduced roll margin; increased stall/approach speed and degraded low-speed handling in the take-off and landing configuration.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to counter roll asymmetry and manage a higher approach speed; possible configuration/abnormal-landing procedure.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric high-lift at low speed is a large reduction in safety margins and low-speed handling capability in the most critical phases. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift augmentation
fha.effAc: No flap/slat augmentation raises stall speed and take-off/landing speeds and distances; flaps-up approach and landing on the semi-prepared strip against the 1,800 m requirement with a predicted rollout margin that assumes normal configuration.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload flying a flaps-up approach and landing; abnormal-configuration performance assessment against available landing distance.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Symmetric loss of high-lift is a significant reduction in functional capability and margins with increased crew workload, absent an asymmetry or loss-of-control effect; the landing-distance margin against 1,800 m governs whether this is more severe and is left for engineering confirmation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground load support
fha.effAc: Reduced ground load-carrying capability (e.g. a bogie/leg unable to carry its share) increases footprint pressure and localised loads on a semi-prepared surface; potential asymmetry or degraded flotation during rollout and taxi.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload managing a degraded ground condition; possible speed/steering limitation on the strip.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition supports a partial-support effect but the aircraft consequence depends on the gear leg/bogie count (preliminary, not frozen) and the flotation/load-path substantiation, which is structural and PRA work not stated in the function; classification cannot be derived here without that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground load support
fha.effAc: Total loss of the ground load path (e.g. gear collapse) leaves the aircraft unsupported on the surface; airframe contact, potential structural damage and loss of the airplane at landing weight.
fha.effCrew: Loss of ground control; evacuation.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A complete loss of ground load support points toward the loss-of-airplane end, but the load-path integrity is a structural/Particular-Risk item the SDD explicitly reserves to structural analysis, not a functional-FHA classification; deriving a class requires the structural substantiation and flight-phase (landing energy) that the function definition does not provide.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded gear retraction
fha.effAc: Uncommanded retraction while the aircraft is on the ground or during the ground roll collapses the ground load path, causing airframe contact and structural damage at landing/take-off weight; in flight it is loss of a commanded gear state affecting configuration.
fha.effCrew: Loss of ground support and directional control; evacuation.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Uncommanded retraction on the ground drives toward a severe ground event, but the classification depends on flight phase (weight-on-wheels vs in-flight) and on whether the WOW/uplock interlocks credited in the SDD prevent it; those are architecture and interlock claims to be tested, not derivable from the function definition, so severity is left for engineering confirmation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent gear extension — uncommanded extension of the landing gear in flight
fha.effAc: Uncommanded gear extension produces a large increase in drag and a nose-down trim change; gear and doors experience aerodynamic loads possibly outside the extension envelope if speed is high; degraded climb/cruise performance and range.
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware through gear position indication and handling change; increased workload to reduce speed within the gear placard, re-plan and manage the abnormal configuration.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded extension gives a significant reduction in performance/functional capability and a significant increase in crew workload with the crew aware and able to slow to the placard; effects support Major rather than Hazardous. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous gear position indication — indication disagrees with true gear state, crew aware of the disagreement
fha.effAc: True gear state is unchanged by the indication itself; the aircraft flies as configured. The hazard is the crew acting on a false indication during approach/landing configuration.
fha.effCrew: Dual dissimilar/independent downlock sensing lets the crew detect a disagreement between the proximity indication and the mechanical visual indicator; increased workload to resolve the true state before landing and to apply the abnormal procedure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on the true gear state the crew acts against (correct-but-shown-wrong vs down-and-locked-shown-up vs up-shown-down) and on landing-without-confirmed-downlock margins; the function definition and SDD do not establish that worst-case landing outcome, so classification cannot be committed here without the landing-configuration effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of gear extension — asymmetric; one or more gear units fail to extend and lock while others are down
fha.effAc: Landing on an incomplete gear set on a semi-prepared surface: asymmetric ground contact, loss of expected flotation and footprint distribution, structural and directional-control consequences on touchdown and rollout within the 1,800 m requirement.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via gear position indication; attempt free-fall alternate extension, then manage a landing in an abnormal gear configuration with high workload and possible off-nominal directional control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is potentially a large reduction in safety margin on a semi-prepared surface landing with an incomplete gear set, but the free-fall alternate extension is an independent recovery path and the SDD does not establish how many units can be affected after alternate extension, nor the touchdown/rollout outcome; the residual-configuration effect is not grounded, so classification cannot be committed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of downlock indication — one of the two independent downlock sensing paths lost, remaining path available
fha.effAc: True gear state unchanged; one of two independent downlock confirmations lost. The remaining independent path still provides downlock confirmation, so a landing can still be made against a confirmed indication.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of the loss of one indication path; slight increase in workload to cross-check the remaining path (proximity vs mechanical visual indicator) and confirm configuration before landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With dual dissimilar independent sensing, loss of one path leaves a confirmed downlock indication and produces at most a slight increase in crew workload and a slight reduction in the confirmation margin; effects support Minor. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded wheel braking — braking applied without crew command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded braking during the take-off roll degrades acceleration and, if asymmetric, induces a directional excursion; on a semi-prepared surface with a 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, an uncommanded application near V1 threatens surface departure or tyre/brake damage.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect, identify and counter an unexpected deceleration or heading deviation; workload increases and a rejected-take-off decision may be forced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect ranges from a minor taxi nuisance to a directional excursion at high ground speed; the SDD does not state whether uncommanded braking can be symmetric-only or asymmetric, nor the achievable brake force per wheel pair without command, so the worst-case aircraft effect (and thus severity) cannot be derived without the braking-control failure envelope. Needs the brake control architecture failure analysis to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous anti-skid response — anti-skid modulates braking incorrectly relative to wheel slip
fha.effAc: Incorrect anti-skid modulation extends stopping distance or causes wheel lock and tyre damage; against the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface, an erroneous response consumes the braking margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew commands braking normally and may not immediately perceive degraded deceleration until stopping performance is evidently short of expectation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Anti-skid is stated as operating per wheel pair but the SDD gives no aircraft-level effect of an erroneous (versus lost) anti-skid response, and this condition is not carried in the project FCIM for SF-009; without the stopping-distance degradation attributable to erroneous anti-skid the aircraft effect cannot be derived. This may be an item-level anti-skid failure mode for the FMEA rather than an AFHA row — confirm scope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of wheel braking — reduced braking capability with no annunciation, crew unaware
fha.effAc: Crew commands normal braking and plans rollout against expected performance; the shortfall manifests only as deceleration below prediction, consuming the margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout and risking overrun off the end of the semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue the landing rollout normally and take no compensating action (no autobrake reversion, no manual increase) until the deficit is physically apparent, by which point remaining surface may be insufficient.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on how much braking is lost undetected and the resulting overrun energy on a semi-prepared surface; the SDD gives the nominal margin (~720 m) but not the deceleration shortfall corresponding to an undetected partial loss, so the worst-case aircraft effect cannot be derived. Needs the braking-degradation-versus-stopping-distance relationship to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of wheel braking — asymmetric — braking retained but reduced and unequal side-to-side
fha.effAc: Asymmetric braking induces a yawing moment during the landing rollout or a rejected take-off, requiring corrective steering/rudder and extending stopping distance; on a semi-prepared strip with a ~720 m nominal margin this threatens a directional excursion or overrun.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via deceleration and heading cues; must apply corrective directional control and may need alternate/accumulator braking, increasing workload during a high-workload phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect spans significant-to-large reduction in stopping/directional capability depending on the asymmetry magnitude and whether dual-supply/accumulator braking recovers it; the SDD confirms dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve but does not quantify the residual asymmetry or its stopping-distance penalty, so severity cannot be derived without the braking degradation envelope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground directional steering
fha.effAc: No nose-wheel steering directional control on the ground; directional control during the ground roll relies on differential braking and rudder effectiveness. On a semi-prepared strip the loss of steering reduces the ability to track the runway centreline and to correct excursions, with potential for a lateral runway excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew maintain directional control with rudder and differential braking; increased workload during ground roll and taxi.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on whether differential braking and rudder authority provide adequate directional control across the ground-speed range on a semi-prepared surface, and on the take-off/landing crosswind and speed cases — the SDD states steering is commanded from tillers and rudder pedals but does not substantiate the residual directional control with steering lost, so the aircraft-level effect cannot be classified without that judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground directional steering
fha.effAc: Reduced ground directional steering authority; centreline tracking and excursion correction remain available but at reduced capability, supplemented by differential braking and rudder.
fha.effCrew: Crew compensate with rudder and differential braking; increased workload during ground roll and taxi.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft-level effect of reduced (versus complete) steering authority depends on the residual steering range and the compensating directional control available on a semi-prepared surface, which the SDD does not substantiate; severity cannot be derived without that engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded ground steering
fha.effAc: Nose-wheel steering deflects without crew command during the ground roll or taxi, producing an uncommanded heading change. At take-off/landing ground speeds on a semi-prepared strip this can drive a lateral excursion off the runway before the crew can counter with rudder and differential braking.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded input and counter it rapidly with opposite steering/rudder and differential braking; high workload, short time to react at speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on the maximum uncommanded steering deflection rate and authority and the crew's ability to counter it within the available distance at take-off/landing speed — the SDD does not state the steering actuator failure authority or rate limits, so the aircraft-level effect cannot be classified without that data and judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ground steering response
fha.effAc: Steering responds to crew command in the wrong sense or magnitude, so a commanded correction produces an incorrect ground-track response. At speed on a semi-prepared strip an erroneous response can worsen rather than correct a deviation, driving a lateral excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive that steering is not responding as expected and must revert to rudder and differential braking; high workload and short time to react at speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the nature and magnitude of the erroneous response and the crew's ability to recover directional control within the available distance — not substantiated in the SDD. Also flag: SF-010-M2 is not present in the current FCIM (only SF-010-M exists); confirm whether an 'erroneous response' condition should exist distinct from 'uncommanded steering'.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded hold access — nose visor unlock/opening not commanded by crew or ground
fha.effAc: On the ground the visor forms the forward structural load path and pressure boundary; uncommanded unlock during ground operation exposes the unsecured-boundary state. In flight the door 'cannot be operated in flight' and a pressure interlock is in series with the unlock command, so an uncommanded full opening is not stated to be credible; the in-flight consequence of an uncommanded UNLOCK (loss of latch/pin engagement) on the pressure boundary and forward load path is not stated in the SDD.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; hold is unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state the in-flight aircraft effect of an uncommanded visor unlock (loss of pressure boundary and forward structural load path). Door operation is inhibited in flight and a pressure interlock is in series with unlock, but the residual consequence of an uncommanded unlock is undetermined here — requires structures / pressurisation determination before a severity is derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous lock status indication — displayed lock status does not match true visor lock state (crew aware via disagreement)
fha.effAc: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and is included in the take-off configuration check; an erroneous indication that disagrees with the dual dissimilar sensing surfaces as a take-off configuration discrepancy, resolvable before take-off.
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware through the dual dissimilar sensing (proximity harness plus mechanical visual indicator) and the take-off configuration monitor, and holds/aborts dispatch until lock state is confirmed; increased crew attention during the configuration check.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is statable (a resolvable configuration-check discrepancy with the crew aware via dual dissimilar sensing), but the aircraft-level consequence is bounded by the masked/latent case which is captured separately in SF-011-M3; severity left for engineer confirm pending the true bounding effect of an erroneous-but-aware indication.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of secured hold access — visor latch/pin engagement lost or incomplete while indicated secure (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Latent unsecured / incompletely locked visor believed secure; the visor forms the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed, so an undetected loss of secured engagement is a latent degradation of that boundary and load path. The SDD does not state the in-flight consequence of an unlatched/unsecured visor.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties taking no action, since both indication paths read secure; no cue to act.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: latent loss of pressure boundary / forward structural load path integrity is a candidate for the top of the scale, but the SDD does not state the in-flight aircraft consequence of an unlatched visor. Requires structures / pressurisation determination (and treatment as a significant latent failure per 14CFR-25.4) before a severity is derived — do not default to the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of hold access — reduced ability to open/close or secure the visor for loading, function still achievable at reduced capability
fha.effAc: Ground-only capability loss: visor operable but at reduced capability (e.g. on the electric backup drive rather than hydraulic), affecting loading/unloading throughput; no stated in-flight aircraft effect.
fha.effCrew: Ground crew works the loading procedure with the aircraft powered from ground supply; longer turnaround. No flight-crew action in flight.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the function is a ground loading/access capability and the SDD states no in-flight aircraft effect for a partial loss; the operating concept frames turnaround/dispatch impact, not a safety-of-flight effect. Severity left empty pending an operational/dispatch effect determination — not a No Safety Effect finding.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of hold access — visor cannot be opened or closed for loading/unloading
fha.effAc: Ground-only capability loss: hold cannot be accessed for loading/unloading; with no line maintenance at the strip this is a dispatch/operational impact. No stated in-flight aircraft effect.
fha.effCrew: No in-flight crew action; ground operation only.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; unoccupied.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: complete loss of hold access is a ground loading capability loss with a dispatch/turnaround consequence; the SDD states no in-flight aircraft-level effect and the door cannot be operated in flight. Severity left empty pending an operational effect determination — not a benign-end default.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous air conditioning and distribution — conditioned air delivered at incorrect temperature, flow or distribution
fha.effAc: Air conditioned or distributed incorrectly to the flight deck and/or hold; effect on the aircraft cannot be bounded from the function definition alone because the same air-cycle bleed feeds pressurisation and the ECS supplies the crew-oxygen logic
fha.effCrew: Potential flight-deck thermal discomfort or workload increase; magnitude depends on the erroneous mode
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: an aircraft effect and its worst-case phase cannot be bounded without knowing whether an erroneous distribution can affect flight-deck habitability, the pressurisation differential, or the crew-oxygen cabin-altitude logic the ECS feeds — the effect must be resolved before a class is committed. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution
fha.effAc: Aircraft loses conditioned-air supply to flight deck and hold; without conditioning the flight deck cannot be held at cabin altitude and a descent to a lower level is required.
fha.effCrew: Crew recognise loss of conditioning/pressurisation via cabin-altitude and ECS indication, don oxygen if cabin altitude rises, and initiate a descent to a safe level; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of conditioning/pressurisation with crew aware, oxygen available and a descent available drives a significant increase in crew workload and a reduction in operating margin, without loss of continued safe flight and landing. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pressure differential
fha.effAc: Outflow control drives the fuselage to a differential not commanded; structure is protected by independent positive and negative pressure relief valves acting independently of the control system.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on flight-deck cabin altitude and on structure depends on the magnitude and direction of the uncommanded excursion and on the preliminary hold differential value (≈8,800 m equivalent), neither of which the SDD bounds; cannot derive a severity without that.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressure differential control
fha.effAc: Control commands an incorrect differential; structure remains protected by the independent positive and negative pressure relief valves.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition is not a listed FCIM malfunction for SF-014 (listed: SF-014-M uncommanded, SF-014-M3 undetected erroneous) and appears to duplicate them; magnitude/direction of the erroneous demand and the preliminary hold differential are unbounded in the SDD, so no aircraft effect can be stated and no severity derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous pressure differential
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential is erroneous and not annunciated; crew continue normal duties and take no action, so the excursion is arrested only by the independent mechanical pressure relief valves.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties and take no corrective action regarding the differential.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The unannunciated case turns on how far the differential can drift before mechanical relief acts and on the preliminary hold differential (≈8,800 m equivalent) — the SDD bounds neither, so the effect on flight-deck cabin altitude and structure cannot be stated and no severity derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pressure differential control
fha.effAc: Reduced pressurisation control capability; one of the two controllers/outflow valves lost, with the pneumatic backup mode able to drive one outflow valve directly on cabin pressure.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe reduced pressurisation function on ECS/cabin-altitude indication; select backup mode or descend as required; some increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With two controllers, two outflow valves and a pneumatic backup either being sufficient, loss of one element leaves the function available and yields at most a slight increase in crew workload; severity proposed for confirmation. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pressure differential control
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential no longer controlled by the pressurisation function; hold is unoccupied and pressurised only to a low differential (≈8,800 m equivalent, preliminary). Independent mechanical relief protects the structure against over/under-pressure.
fha.effCrew: Flight deck loses controlled cabin altitude; crew don oxygen masks and initiate descent to a breathable altitude; increased workload managing an off-nominal pressurisation state and diversion.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of differential control on an unoccupied-hold, low-differential aircraft drives a crew descent/diversion with increased workload; independent mechanical relief protects structure. Preliminary hold differential is the load-bearing driver — confirm against the frozen value and the crew-oxygen diversion basis before committing; could rise if breathable-altitude descent is not assured. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent ice protection
fha.effAc: Ice protection operates when not required; wing anti-ice bleed demand reduces environmental pack capacity and imposes a performance penalty that is applied automatically to displayed performance.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe the applied performance penalty and bleed demand; slight increase in workload to manage/deselect an un-needed protection mode.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent activation manifests as a performance penalty and reduced pack capacity that are annunciated and automatically applied to displayed performance; a slight workload increase with no reduction in safety margins. Confirm the pack-capacity reduction does not itself force a conditioning limit before committing. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice protection
fha.effPax: No passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft effect: the provided functions do not state the icing-envelope exposure, which protected surfaces are lost in the partial case, or the residual crew-detection basis needed to establish the effect of degraded accretion protection. Needs the icing certification-basis envelope and the partial-loss coverage to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ice protection
fha.effPax: No passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aware complete-loss case: with detection advisory and manual selection available, the aircraft effect depends on the icing-envelope exposure and the assumed crew action (exit icing conditions) — neither is stated in the provided functions. Needs the icing certification-basis envelope and the assumed crew avoidance action to derive an effect and classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ice protection
fha.effAc: Ice protection is lost while the crew remain unaware and take no action; ice accretes on unprotected surfaces, inlets and probes, degrading aerodynamic performance and potentially probe/detection integrity while the aircraft continues in the icing envelope.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties with no annunciation of the protection loss; the failure is caught only when accretion effects become manifest, by which time margins may already be eroded.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected loss allows accretion in the icing envelope with the crew taking no compensating action, giving a large reduction in safety margins; proposed pending the icing-envelope exposure and any independent monitoring that would bound continued exposure. Confirm against the icing certification basis before committing — could be Catastrophic if accretion is unbounded, or lower if detection provides an independent alert. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of probe heat
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded on the SF-016 function 'Protect probes and detect icing' as captured: the SF-016 FCIM enumerates ice-detection conditions only and does not carry a probe-heat-loss condition. An aircraft effect for undetected loss of probe heat is an air-data / flight-information integrity outcome; the provided SF-016 definition does not substantiate its aircraft effect. Missing: the function that owns probe heating and its detection provisions, and the air-data consequence of unheated probes.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to detect icing — icing present, no detection or advisory, crew unaware and take no action
fha.effAc: With the crew unaware, ice protection is not manually selected and (if in automatic) is not commanded on; ice accretes on unprotected surfaces, degrading lift/drag, control effectiveness and potentially probe accuracy, with reduction in safety margins that can worsen with exposure time.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties with no cue that icing is present; the failure defeats the advisory that would otherwise prompt protection or exit from the icing condition.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Proposed severity is not committed because the magnitude of the safety-margin reduction depends on the certification icing envelope and on whether automatic activation is armed — neither is quantified in the provided context. Missing: the icing envelope of the certification basis and the assumed detector/auto-activation state, which drive whether this is Major or Hazardous.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of probe heat
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Duplicate probe-heat condition (see SF-016-M2): cannot be grounded on the SF-016 'detect icing' function as captured; the SF-016 FCIM carries no probe-heat condition. Missing: the owning function for probe heating and its air-data integrity consequence. Flagged for your disposition as a possible duplicate of SF-016-M2.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ice detection
fha.effAc: No ice-accretion detection available; ice protection can still be selected and run manually at any time, so protective capability is retained but automatic-on and detection advisory are lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew must monitor for icing conditions by external cues and TAT/OAT and manage ice protection manually, increasing workload and vigilance in the icing envelope.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of detection with protection still manually available is a significant increase in crew workload and reduced situational awareness in icing, not a loss of protection; confirm against the icing certification basis and the ice-protection allocation. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous flight and navigation information (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Primary flight/navigation information is erroneous; crew becomes aware through disagreement against the independent standby instrument and reverts to standby, at reduced capability and reduced margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects the discrepancy, cross-checks the independent standby attitude/airspeed/altitude, reverts and manages the flight with significantly increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous primary flight/navigation information detected by the crew produces a large reduction in safety margins and excessive workload while reverting to standby; awareness is credited via the independent standby instrument. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous flight and navigation information (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Misleading primary flight/navigation information is not detected; crew continue normal duties acting on corrupted data, which can drive the aircraft outside safe flight margins with no cue to intervene.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally taking no corrective action, acting on erroneous information as though valid.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary flight/navigation information acted upon can lead to loss of the aeroplane; severity classed at function level implementation-agnostic — the independent standby and dissimilar sources are mitigating architecture to be substantiated in the PSSA. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of flight and navigation information
fha.effAc: Some flight/navigation information is lost while the remainder is available; reduced display/sensor capability with reversion to remaining sources at reduced margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew reconfigures to remaining sources and manages the flight on reduced information with increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss of flight/navigation information reverting to remaining valid sources is a significant reduction in capability and increase in crew workload; confirm which information is lost against the AVI redundancy allocation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation information
fha.effAc: All primary flight/navigation information is lost; the aircraft is flown on the independent standby instrument only, a survivable but degraded means with a large reduction in safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew reverts to the independent standby attitude/airspeed/altitude and flies a degraded configuration with excessive workload, particularly at night or in IMC.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of primary flight/navigation information leaving only the independent standby instrument is a large reduction in safety margins and excessive crew workload; confirm the standby-only case adequacy in IMC against the AVI architecture. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous crew alerting — misprioritised (alerts presented in the wrong priority order within the consolidated list)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD describes a 'single prioritised crew alert list' but does not define the consequence of an incorrect priority ordering distinct from general erroneous alerting; this condition is not carried in the SF-018 FCIM (only SF-018-M exists). Without a stated behaviour for how a misprioritised alert alters crew response, an aircraft effect cannot be grounded and severity cannot be derived. Missing: the aircraft-level effect of misprioritisation (e.g. whether a higher-priority alert is masked/delayed).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge
fha.effAc: Uncommanded bottle discharge into a nacelle depletes agent; if the affected engine is healthy no immediate performance loss, but suppression capacity for a genuine subsequent fire in that engine pair is reduced given two bottles cross-plumbed per pair.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to discharge status; assess and manage reduced suppression reserve.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SF-019-M2 is not an existing FCIM condition under SF-019 (the model holds SF-019-M 'Erroneous fire or overheat detection'); reconcile the FCIM before committing severity. Classification also depends on whether both bottles or one can inadvertently discharge and on whether a subsequent fire is credited concurrently — not resolvable from the function definition alone.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of extinguishing capability (fire detection retained)
fha.effAc: Reduced extinguishing agent available; a fire in an engine nacelle or the APU compartment may not be fully extinguished on first discharge, reducing the margin against an uncontrolled/continuing fire.
fha.effCrew: Crew are alerted to fire by retained detection and actuate the fire handle(s) as normal, but a discharge may be ineffective or insufficient; increased workload managing a continuing fire and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects show a significant reduction in the safety margin against a continuing fire with detection retained (crew aware and acting); not a large reduction because detection and partial extinguishing remain. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire detection and extinguishing
fha.effAc: No means to detect fire/overheat in the protected zones (engine nacelles, APU) and no means to extinguish; an in-zone fire can develop and propagate undetected and unchecked, a large reduction in the safety margin against fire.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no fire warning and have no extinguishing means; unable to take timely action against an engine or APU fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of both detection and extinguishing in fire zones is a large reduction in functional capability/safety margins against fire; classified Hazardous pending confirmation of the credible fire-progression outcome. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew breathing oxygen
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; reduced oxygen reserve available to the flight crew for a depressurisation, smoke or fume event and the subsequent descent/diversion.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain oxygen at reduced reserve (one cylinder / crossover); adequate for the required duration at reduced margin, with increased workload managing the reduced reserve during a diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen provided; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced-reserve oxygen still supports the crew for the required diversion, a significant reduction in safety margin at the maximum operating altitude; not Hazardous because a workable reserve remains. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen — crew aware
fha.effAc: No breathing oxygen available to the flight crew for a depressurisation, smoke or fume event; aircraft depends on emergency descent to a breathable altitude for continued safe flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew become aware via displayed cylinder pressure / low-pressure alerting; initiate emergency descent, but have no protection against smoke/fumes and no oxygen at high cabin altitude before reaching a breathable level, risking impairment of task performance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With crew aware and descending, effects support a large reduction in safety margins / crew impairment on a coincident depressurisation or smoke event; Hazardous pending confirmation of the credible worst-case event coincidence. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen — crew unaware
fha.effAc: No breathing oxygen available and no crew awareness of the loss; on a coincident depressurisation or smoke/fume event the crew attempt to don masks and find no oxygen, with no time to react at high cabin altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally, unaware of the loss; discover it only on attempting to use the masks during a depressurisation or smoke event, at which point incapacitation can follow with no available protection.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Crew-unaware total loss coincident with a depressurisation or smoke/fume event can incapacitate the two-crew flight deck with no recovery means; effects support Catastrophic pending confirmation of event coincidence and detection assumptions. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of gear extension — landing gear cannot be extended and locked down by any means (normal, alternate free-fall, or manual)
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be configured for a normal landing; a gear-up or partial-gear landing results with substantial airframe damage and departure from the semi-prepared surface likely at landing weight up to 318,000 kg.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via downlock indication; execute abnormal/emergency landing procedure and prepare for a gear-up arrival, elevated workload throughout approach and landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Free-fall alternate extension is provided independent of hydraulic pressure, so a complete loss of extension by every means is a large reduction in functional capability with elevated crew workload but a survivable arrival — HAZ-1. Confirm whether any credible scenario escalates to loss of the airplane (CAT-1); if so this row is Catastrophic. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking
fha.effAc: No wheel braking available on any wheel; deceleration on the ground relies on remaining means (reverse thrust on inboard engines, aerodynamic drag). On the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout at maximum landing weight, loss of all wheel braking removes the primary deceleration means and can result in a runway/strip overrun; a rejected take-off near V1 with no braking is unstoppable within the available distance.
fha.effCrew: Crew recognise loss of braking and apply remaining deceleration means; high workload and reduced options on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An overrun off a semi-prepared strip at landing/RTO speeds with no braking can lead to loss of the airplane; per Table A6 CAT-1. Severity is PROPOSED — depends on the credited deceleration contribution of the two inboard reversers and the semi-prepared surface braking model, which are preliminary in the SDD. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of payload restraint — reduced strap tension or loss at one station, remaining stations carry the load
fha.effAc: Reduced restraint margin on a single 72.6 t blade; a lost strap at one station is designed to be carried by its neighbours, so the blade remains restrained but with reduced margin against the flight-load envelope; annunciated to the crew
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to a restraint condition and manages the flight within a reduced load envelope; increased monitoring and possible manoeuvre limitation
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in restraint margin on the sizing payload with the load still carried and the crew alerted, per MAJ-1 significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of payload restraint — reduced tension at one or more stations not annunciated, crew continue normally
