fha.effAc: Restraint margin on the 72.6 t blade degraded without crew awareness; the crew take no restraint-related action and fly the full load envelope on a load path already below its designed margin, so a subsequent load event can propagate to loss of restraint or structural overload
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties and take no action regarding the degraded restraint
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Latent reduction in restraint margin on the sizing payload flown at full envelope without crew awareness or compensating action, giving a large reduction in functional capability per HAZ-1; whether an undetected station loss can progress to complete loss depends on the tension-loop coverage the SDD records as an open item [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of payload restraint — the 72.6 t blade is no longer restrained along the full hold length
fha.effAc: A single unitised 72.6 t item free to shift over the 108 m hold produces a large and uncontrollable centre-of-gravity excursion and imposes loads the hold floor hard points and airframe are not designed to carry, leading to loss of the aircraft
fha.effCrew: Rapid uncontrollable CG shift beyond the recoverable envelope; crew action cannot restore control
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An unrestrained 72.6 t single item shifting over the full 108 m hold drives a CG excursion and structural loading consistent with loss of the airplane per CAT-1 [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of air conditioning and distribution — reduced conditioning capacity, e.g. single-pack operation
fha.effAc: Reduced conditioning capacity; single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule, so the aircraft continues with degraded flight-deck and hold conditioning
fha.effCrew: Possible increase in flight-deck workload or discomfort under a reduced conditioning schedule
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-pack operation is an anticipated degraded mode the design permits with a reduced hold schedule, giving at most a slight increase in crew workload or discomfort per MIN-2 / MIN-3; confirm the flight-deck habitability effect supports Minor rather than Major [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ice detection — icing indicated (or ice protection auto-commanded) when no icing exists
fha.effAc: Ice protection may auto-activate without accretion, imposing the wing anti-ice performance penalty and reducing pack capacity when not required; no loss of any protected surface. False detection alone does not degrade aircraft handling.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive a spurious icing advisory; slight increase in workload to cross-check ice detection against actual conditions and manage bleed/performance penalty. Detection is advisory and manual override is available at any time.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated support a slight increase in crew workload and a performance penalty without loss of a required capability; MIN-2. Detection is advisory with manual selection always available, so an erroneous advisory does not by itself reduce safety margins. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice detection — one of the two ice detectors unavailable, reduced detection coverage/redundancy
fha.effAc: Detection continues on the remaining detector; coverage/redundancy is reduced but icing can still be sensed and protection selected. No immediate loss of a protected surface; manual selection remains available at any time.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; slight increase in workload to monitor conditions and select protection manually rather than relying on full automatic detection.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated support a slight reduction in redundancy with a slight increase in crew workload while detection and manual protection remain available; MIN-1/MIN-2. Confirm against the assumed icing exposure — a longer exposure with a single detector could warrant re-examination. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting — no consolidated fault/warning annunciation available to the crew (aware: absence of the alerting list is itself apparent)
fha.effAc: No failure or configuration event is annunciated; subsequent system failures accrue undetected until they manifest through other symptoms or direct effects.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses the single prioritised alert list and its associated procedures; must monitor raw parameters and infer failures unaided, materially increasing workload and the chance a significant failure is missed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the sole consolidated alerting means removes the crew's primary awareness of failures across all systems; latent subsequent failures accruing undetected is a large reduction in safety margin and imposes excessive workload/impairment on the crew (HAZ-1/HAZ-2). Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew alerting — a subset of alerts or one alerting channel unavailable, some annunciation still provided
fha.effAc: A subset of system status/warnings is not annunciated; failures within the affected coverage accrue undetected while the remainder of the alerting function operates.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains partial alerting but cannot rely on complete coverage; increased monitoring workload and risk that a failure in the unannunciated subset is missed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced but not absent alerting coverage is a significant reduction in the crew's failure-awareness capability with a significant workload increase, short of the Hazardous case where all consolidated alerting is lost (MAJ-1/MAJ-2). Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous crew alerting — a false or incorrect alert presented (annunciating a failure that has not occurred, or the wrong condition)
fha.effAc: Aircraft state is nominal but presented as failed; crew may action a procedure inappropriately (e.g. shut down a healthy system), potentially degrading available capability.
fha.effCrew: Crew responds to a false or incorrect alert, taking action against a healthy system; distraction and misdirected workload, with the possibility of an inappropriate configuration change.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false/incorrect alert can drive an inappropriate crew action and a significant workload increase, but the true aircraft state remains nominal and other cues remain available; significant increase in crew workload (MAJ-1/MAJ-2). Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected suppression of a valid alert — a genuine alert is inhibited or not presented, and the suppression is itself undetected (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: A real failure or hazardous condition occurs but is not annunciated; the crew continue normally and take no action, so the underlying failure develops unmitigated and may combine with further failures.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the suppressed condition; continue their duties normally and take no mitigating action, allowing an unaddressed failure to progress.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Silent suppression of a valid alert defeats the crew's awareness of a real failure with no compensating cue from the alerting function itself; an unmitigated developing failure represents a large reduction in safety margin (HAZ-1). Severity of the specific suppressed condition could drive higher — retained for engineer review of the worst credible suppressed alert. Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of crew alerting
fha.effAc: Aircraft continues without the consolidated prioritised alerting that annunciates system failures; a subsequent failure that relies on alerting to prompt crew action goes unannunciated.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware alerting is lost; a failure requiring a procedural response is not flagged, defeating the assumed crew mitigation for other conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Latent loss of alerting removes the crew-detection layer assumed by other failure conditions; combined with a subsequent failure it produces a large reduction in safety margins (HAZ-1). Engineer to confirm; §25.4 significant-latent-failure treatment applies. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous fire or overheat detection
fha.effAc: False fire/overheat warning may prompt engine shutdown, fire-handle actuation and extinguishant discharge on a healthy engine, reducing available thrust; on a four-engine aircraft with engine-out capability the aircraft remains controllable.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to a valid-appearing warning with the shutdown/discharge procedure; increased workload and a potentially unnecessary thrust reduction and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Unnecessary shutdown of one healthy engine with retained flight on remaining engines gives a significant reduction in functional capability and increased crew workload (MAJ-1/MAJ-2). Engineer to confirm; worst applicable phase governs. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of fire detection
fha.effAc: Fire/overheat in a monitored zone (engine nacelle, APU, bleed duct run, gear bay or hold) is not annunciated; an undetected fire can propagate uncontained toward critical structure or systems before any crew response.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware detection is lost; the extinguishing action assumed to follow detection is never initiated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Latent loss of detection defeats the detect-then-extinguish protection for fire zones; an undetected, unfought fire can lead to loss of the aircraft (CAT-1). Engineer to confirm; §25.4 significant-latent-failure treatment applies given latency combined with a fire event. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire detection and extinguishing
fha.effAc: Loss of one detection loop degrades to single-loop logic; or loss of one extinguisher bottle reduces suppression reserve for an engine pair. Detection/suppression remains available at reduced redundancy for a single subsequent event.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the degraded state; may apply a dispatch or operational limitation; increased vigilance for the affected zone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced redundancy in the fire-protection layer is a significant reduction in a safety-related functional capability while the protective function itself remains available (MAJ-1). Engineer to confirm; whether a concurrent fire is credited affects the worst-case phase. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: Fuel, hydraulic, electrical and wiring systems are resources, not aircraft functions, and are excluded from this decomposition.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD inventory explicitly tags four systems as resources rather than functions, and the modeling rule bars authoring resources as functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any of these must be captured as a behavioural function, an additional top-level function and its sub-functions would be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS from the function set.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.text: The nose-door load path and hold-floor hard points are structure and are excluded from the functional decomposition.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD calls the door a single load path treated as structure and the hold hard points as having no functional redundancy; structure is out of scope for a functional FHA.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the safety team elects to functionalise structural integrity, those items move to structural analysis / PRA rather than these function rows regardless.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion note on 'Provide and secure hold access' and 'Restrain the payload' sub-functions.

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: Combining fire protection and crew oxygen under one top-level function is an acceptable aircraft-level grouping.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes FPR and OXY as separate systems with distinct purposes; grouping them is an analyst choice not fixed by the document.
assumptions.ifWrong: If separated, this becomes two top-level functions each carrying its single sub-function; no failure condition or independence claim changes.
assumptions.usedFor: Top function 'Protect against fire and provide crew oxygen' and its two sub-functions.

citations.quote: detects fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected, and provides the means to extinguish

assumptions.text: The crew-Unaware variant applies only to the erroneous/uncommanded conditions of the control-axis functions, whose slow onset can develop below the crew's detection threshold, while total and partial loss of control are self-evident and carry no unaware row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states degraded laws and jam/asymmetry discretes are annunciated but does not establish detection thresholds for slow-onset erroneous surface motion, so the awareness split for malfunctions cannot be fully grounded from functions alone.
assumptions.ifWrong: If slow-onset erroneous/uncommanded axis motion is in fact always annunciated, the SF-003/004/005 Unaware rows collapse and only the Aware rows remain.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003/SF-004/SF-005 Unaware rows (Undetected erroneous / Undetected uncommanded control)

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

assumptions.text: Ground deceleration thrust is a distinct aircraft function delivered by the inboard reversers and its inadvertent-in-flight case is prevented by the WOW/radio-altimeter inhibit rather than eliminated as a condition.
assumptions.rationale: The reverse-thrust capability is described only within Propulsion, so its treatment as the SF-002 function and the retention of an inadvertent-deployment malfunction rests on reading the inhibit as a mitigation, not a removal of the condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If SF-002 is not carried as a separate aircraft function or the in-flight inadvertent case is deemed non-credible, the SF-002 inadvertent malfunction entry is removed.

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.text: Asymmetric partial loss of forward thrust is retained as a distinct condition from symmetric partial loss because the outboard-engine moment arm makes the directional consequence the sizing case.
assumptions.rationale: The function list gives only 'provide forward thrust'; splitting partial loss into symmetric and asymmetric leans on the SDD's statement that asymmetric outboard thrust sizes directional control.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetric loss is not carried separately, the SF-001 partials[] collapse to a single partial-loss condition.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 partials[] (symmetric / asymmetric partial loss of forward thrust)

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: High-lift asymmetry can develop below crew detection thresholds, warranting a crew-Unaware malfunction variant for SF-006.

assumptions.rationale: The FHA needs an occupant-effect column, and the SDD's occupancy statement is what fixes it for every SF-013/SF-014 row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the hold were occupied, occupant-effect and severity for every pressurisation row would rise, likely to Hazardous or Catastrophic for the loss/undetected-erroneous cases.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-013-TL, SF-014-M, SF-014-M2, SF-014-M3, SF-014-PL

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: The hold pressurisation differential (≈8,800 m hold-altitude equivalent) is preliminary and its magnitude is not yet bounded for failure analysis.
assumptions.rationale: The severity of uncommanded/erroneous differential turns on how far the fuselage can drift, which the preliminary value does not bound.
assumptions.ifWrong: A frozen differential could support classifying SF-014-M/M2/M3 (currently left empty); a high differential could push the undetected-erroneous case toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: empty severity on SF-014-M, SF-014-M2, SF-014-M3

citations.quote: The hold differential is preliminary design data and is not frozen.

assumptions.text: Independent positive and negative mechanical relief valves arrest a pressure excursion regardless of control-system state.
assumptions.rationale: The uncommanded/undetected-erroneous effect statements lean on mechanical relief being the backstop for structural protection.
assumptions.ifWrong: If relief protection is not independent or is insufficient, SF-014-M/M3 could reach structural-failure severity (Hazardous/Catastrophic).

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.

assumptions.text: The pneumatic backup and second controller/outflow valve remain available for the SF-014-PL partial-loss case.
assumptions.rationale: The Minor proposal for SF-014-PL rests on redundancy leaving the function available after loss of one element.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the partial loss removes both the redundant valve and the backup, SF-014-PL rises to Major or higher.

citations.quote: two digital controllers driving two outflow valves, either valve being sufficient. A pneumatic backup mode

assumptions.text: A descent to a lower flight level is available following loss of conditioning/pressurisation, supported by crew oxygen for the descent.
assumptions.rationale: The Major proposal for SF-013-TL rests on crew awareness plus an available descent and oxygen, keeping the outcome short of loss of continued safe flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If descent or crew oxygen is not available, SF-013-TL could rise to Hazardous.

citations.quote: breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and for the descent

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and only the flight deck is a pressurised occupied volume, so pressurisation-loss effects fall on the crew, not passengers.
assumptions.rationale: The functions list gives no occupancy model; the SDD states the hold is unoccupied, which is load-bearing for SF-014-TL effects and severity.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the hold were occupied, SF-014-TL passenger/occupant effects and severity would rise toward Hazardous or Catastrophic.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: Independent mechanical over/under-pressure relief remains available on complete loss of the pressure-differential control function.
assumptions.rationale: The provided functions do not describe protection redundancy; the SDD credits independent relief, which bounds the structural effect of SF-014-TL.
assumptions.ifWrong: If relief is not independent of the control function, SF-014-TL could involve a structural over-pressure and escalate to Hazardous/Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.

assumptions.text: The maximum operating altitude and low hold differential permit descent to a breathable altitude within crew-oxygen endurance after loss of pressurisation control.
assumptions.rationale: No diversion/endurance data is in the functions; the SDD's FL260 ceiling and crew-oxygen sizing underlie the assumed survivable descent for SF-014-TL.
assumptions.ifWrong: If descent to a breathable altitude is not assured within oxygen endurance, SF-014-TL severity rises above Major.

citations.quote: Maximum operating altitude FL260

assumptions.text: Undetected loss of ice protection occurs while the aircraft is within the icing envelope of the certification basis with no independent alert of the loss.
assumptions.rationale: The functions do not state icing exposure; the proposed Hazardous class for SF-015-TL2 depends on continued exposure with the crew unaware.
assumptions.ifWrong: If accretion is unbounded, SF-015-TL2 could be Catastrophic; if an independent detector alerts the crew, it drops toward Major.

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available; the system may also be selected on manually

assumptions.text: Ice detection is advisory with manual selection available at any time, so an erroneous or degraded detection does not by itself remove a required protection capability.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection is advisory and manually selectable, but does not state whether automatic activation is armed by default in service, which governs the M3 and M/PL effects.
assumptions.ifWrong: If automatic activation is the sole means and manual backup is not routinely used, SF-016-M3 escalates and SF-016-M/PL workload effects change.

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available; the system may also be selected on manually at any time.

assumptions.text: SF-016 'Protect probes and detect icing' as captured in the model owns ice detection only, not probe-heating integrity, so 'undetected loss of probe heat' has no grounded aircraft effect under this function.
assumptions.rationale: The SF-016 FCIM rows enumerate ice-detection conditions only; the two probe-heat conditions this turn are not represented there, forcing abstention on their aircraft effect.
assumptions.ifWrong: If SF-016 does own probe heating, SF-016-M2/M4 gain an air-data integrity effect and a non-empty severity, and are no longer candidate duplicates.

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually.

assumptions.text: SF-016-M4 is a duplicate of SF-016-M2 (both 'Undetected loss of probe heat').
assumptions.rationale: The two conditions carry identical wording in this turn's list; without distinguishing context they cannot be told apart from the provided material.
assumptions.ifWrong: If they are distinct conditions, each needs its own effect and severity once the owning function is identified.

assumptions.text: An independent integrated standby instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays remains available for the aware-erroneous, total-loss and partial-loss flight/navigation cases.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the standby exists but the AFHA is implementation-agnostic and does not confirm it survives the same events as the primary; awareness/reversion credit rests on it.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-017-M, SF-017-PL and SF-017-TL severities would worsen (potentially toward Catastrophic) if no independent reversion means exists.

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: For SF-017-M2 the erroneous primary information is misleading in a way not caught by the crew before it affects the flight path (no timely standby cross-check).
assumptions.rationale: The unaware condition per ARP4761A assumes the crew take no corrective action; whether the standby disagreement is noticed is a detection question deferred to the PSSA.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a monitor/standby reliably annunciates the disagreement, SF-017-M2 collapses into the aware case (SF-017-M) and severity reduces to Hazardous.

assumptions.text: Ice detection on the HL-1 is advisory only with manual selection of ice protection available at any time, so loss of detection does not remove ice-protection capability.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes detection as advisory with manual on; the FHA severity for SF-016-TL depends on protection remaining manually available.
assumptions.ifWrong: If ice protection depends on detection to activate, SF-016-TL severity increases substantially (toward Hazardous) in the icing envelope.

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available; the system may also be selected on manually

assumptions.text: The unoccupied hold means no in-flight passenger/occupant is exposed to any SF-018 alerting failure.
assumptions.rationale: The AFHA occupant-effect column requires an occupant exposure; the SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight and the crew is the only complement.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants are carried in flight, the occupant-effect column and possibly the severity of the suppression/loss cases would need re-evaluation.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-018-TL, PL, M, M2, M3

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: Complete loss of the consolidated alerting list removes the crew's only primary means of failure awareness, so subsequent failures accrue undetected.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD presents alerting as a single consolidated list; it does not describe an independent secondary alerting means that would preserve awareness on total loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an independent backup awareness path exists, SF-018-TL and SF-018-M3 severities could be lower than Hazardous.

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.text: An undetected loss of fire detection is combined with an actual fire event in a monitored zone when assessing SF-019-M3 severity.
assumptions.rationale: The function definition names detection but not the outcome of an undetected fire; classifying the latent condition requires positing the subsequent fire it fails to catch.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a latent detection loss is not credited against a concurrent fire, SF-019-M3 severity falls below Catastrophic toward Hazardous/Major.

citations.quote: detects fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected, and provides the means to extinguish

assumptions.text: Erroneous fire/overheat detection leads the crew to shut down and discharge on one healthy engine, with the remaining engines sustaining flight.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states extinguishing is a crew action via the fire handles but does not state the aircraft-level outcome of a false warning; the effect must be posited to classify.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a false warning does not credibly cause an unnecessary shutdown, SF-019-M severity drops toward Minor; if it can cause multiple shutdowns, it rises.

citations.quote: Extinguishing in the engine and APU zones is a crew action through the fire handles

assumptions.text: Loss of crew alerting is latent (undetected) and other failure conditions rely on alerting-prompted crew action as their mitigation.
assumptions.rationale: The condition is the unaware variant; its severity depends on alerting being the assumed detection layer for other conditions, which the FCIM awareness splits imply but the function definition does not state.
assumptions.ifWrong: If alerting is independently monitored/annunciated or other conditions do not depend on it, SF-018-TL2 severity drops below Hazardous.

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.text: SF-019-M2 (Inadvertent extinguishant discharge) should exist as a distinct SF-019 malfunction condition despite not being in the current FCIM.
assumptions.rationale: The turn instructs a row for SF-019-M2 but the model's SF-019 FCIM malfunction cell holds only 'Erroneous fire or overheat detection'; the mismatch blocks a grounded severity.
assumptions.ifWrong: If SF-019-M2 is not a valid condition, the row should be deleted rather than classified; if it is, the FCIM must be updated to carry it.

citations.quote: two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so that either bottle can discharge into either nacelle

assumptions.text: A loss of crew breathing oxygen is assessed coincident with a credible depressurisation, smoke or fume event within the same flight.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the oxygen function exists for these events but provides no exposure/coincidence basis; classifying SF-020 conditions requires assuming the demand event that makes oxygen loss consequential.
assumptions.ifWrong: If oxygen loss is assessed with no coincident demand event, SF-020-TL and SF-020-TL2 severities drop and the Hazardous/Catastrophic classifications no longer hold.

citations.quote: supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events

assumptions.text: For SF-020-TL2 the crew do not detect the oxygen loss before it is needed, i.e. the displayed cylinder pressure / dispatch check does not catch the failure that develops in flight.
assumptions.rationale: Cylinder pressure is displayed and is a dispatch item, so the unaware variant only holds for an in-flight loss that escapes crew monitoring; the SDD does not state monitoring coverage in flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the loss is always annunciated/detected in flight, SF-020-TL2 collapses into the aware SF-020-TL case and the Catastrophic proposal is not supported.

citations.quote: Cylinder pressure is displayed continuously on the flight deck and is a dispatch item.

assumptions.text: The maximum operating altitude of FL260 sets the cabin-altitude exposure and time-of-useful-consciousness margin relevant to crew oxygen loss.
assumptions.rationale: Severity of oxygen loss depends on altitude exposure; the SDD gives FL260 but no cabin-altitude-versus-time analysis, so the altitude figure is taken as the driving parameter.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the effective cabin-altitude exposure is lower/higher than assumed, the SF-020 severities shift accordingly.

assumptions.text: The fire zones requiring detection and extinguishing (engine nacelles, APU) present a credible in-flight fire whose progression, absent detection/extinguishing, threatens the airframe.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the protected fire zones but does not analyse fire progression; the SF-019 severities assume a fire in these zones can develop consequentially without protection.
assumptions.ifWrong: If credible fire progression in the unprotected zones is benign, SF-019-TL Hazardous and SF-019-PL2 Major would reduce.
